name: Marl & Cane
oneLiner: A single-vineyard estate whose page follows the juice out of the fruit: 140 scrubbed frames of three chained beats — a heap of whole grapes giving way and bleeding across concrete, the stream falling into a bottle, the glass filling — with the year's one decision underneath.

axes.secondaryReason: the spec left D's secondary an open draw between physics-interaction and brutalist-raw, and the motion budget decided it: physics would have been a SECOND motion system competing with the scroll spine for one clock (Morningside's argument, reused because it is correct), while brutalist-raw costs zero motion budget because it lives in structure, type and the flat presentation of numbers. It is also the sharpest refusal of what the look-first sweep found the category defaults to — oxblood, gilt rules and a centred Didone selling a bottle — and concrete is a real winery material rather than a conceit. The founder's own counterweight rule is satisfied structurally: the page's entire hero is a living plant in raking sunlight, so brutalism is the frame around the nature and never the subject
axes.portfolioNew: checked against all 24 shipped site.json files in both orderings — no site pairs otherworldly-animation with brutalist-raw, and the unordered set {otherworldly, brutalist} appears nowhere

paletteSeed: an ACHROMATIC page holding exactly one chromatic event — bone ground, near-black ink, and a single accent whose HUE is measured off the frames the scrub is showing. The arc means something: the whole fruit reads cool blue-violet (250 degrees) and the page WARMS to garnet (355 then 12 then 22) as the juice is let out of it, so the colour is released by the crush rather than applied to the page. Lightness is solved per hue for a constant 4.85:1 on bone, because a fixed lightness fails AA somewhere on any hue sweep.
typeDirection: Syne (variable) for display — a contemporary, slightly strange face with an art-institution register rather than a winery one, chosen to refuse the high-contrast Didone the vertical defaults to — against Geist and Geist Mono for everything the estate states as fact: the vintage figures, the chapter marks, the ripening table and the chart's ticks. The mono is the deliberate inversion of Morningside's 'no monospace' rule and for the same underlying reason: that page's differentiation was NOT being an instrument, and this one's is that it carries a laboratory record. All three OFL, all three portfolio-new, all vendored locally
motionBudget: ONE scroll clock and no second animation system: 140 scrubbed frames across THREE Seedance takes — the crush (a transformation, two registered keyframes), the bottle fill and the glass (both POURS, which are CYCLES, so single start frames and no registration risk at all). Five chapter anchors (0 · 36 · 71 · 99 · 139) whose spans are DERIVED from the frames each drives at 34px/frame desktop and 25px/frame touch; measured in a browser at 42-54px per frame with no frame starved and none unreachable. The first chapter drives NO frames on purpose — it holds frame 0 until the stage is on screen, because without that runway the first eight frames are spent where nobody can see them. Each take's live range is measured and recorded in the manifest, so the dead tails are never spent on scroll. Reduced-motion gets discrete states; no-JS gets the full chart, every chapter and one lit frame.

verdict.note: Site D of the landing arc and the last site in it. FIRST BUILD REJECTED BY THE FOUNDER (s112): it shipped an 81-frame veraison time-lapse, and his verdict was 'i think you didnt need a transition video of the grape turning ripe ... did you not learn that my taste is not precise or scientific but imaginative and abstract'. He supplied the replacement himself — grapes, bursting for their juice, the juice into a bottle, poured into a glass — and that is what this page now is. The distinction the meta-prompt now carries: a TIME-LAPSE documents a subject while nature acts on it; a JOURNEY follows a material through states to a payoff. Morningside (which he praised) is a journey; veraison was a time-lapse. Copy cut 851 -> 371 words on the same review ('dont be too wordy or verbose'), against a 628-site median and morningside's 594, and the budget is now an executable ratchet. The wine-glass still he flagged for compression was dropped entirely — the pour sequence shows the glass, so the photograph was redundant.
